limits: One selected cleaning system; the other five annual cells are not simultaneously executed.
Outside reservations are unavailable capacity, not inferred workloads, fulfilled commitments, resource cash or employment.
Prior use is an explicit opening balance for the partial first year, not reconstructed historical activity; January openings require zero prior-window use.
The annual budget and monthly allocation are both necessary ceilings. Unused monthly capacity does not waive either.
Support includes software qualification. Commissioning consumes the separate integration pool and same-month support.
Existing deterministic physical order gives installed support priority over new commissioning; this is not an optimized allocation.
A failed contingent funding group consumes no annual booking. Fixed staffing, subscriptions, debt and other obligations still follow their existing contracts.
All numerical assumptions remain synthetic; no target annual staffing plan, allocation contract or service economics are measured.
Typed qualified parts and share entry are joined here. One target architecture is joined; asset recovery and endogenous learning remain separate.
Shared provider support/integration ceilings do not pool separate operating-company site crews or legal cash accounts.

replacement_outcomes.scope: one declared calendar replacement, conditional on the named unit existing; not a measured failure process

component_inventory.cash_boundary: Components are supplier-funded/consigned until paid issue. Manufacturing/support bundles include consumed materials once; no new bill is added. Opening stocks and supplier financing before issue are outside the window.
component_inventory.maintenance_boundary: One explicit replacement requirement per named unit. Its labor is assumed within the existing support booking and allocation. Fractional annual spare rates do not set its date, probability, labor or cost.
component_inventory.annual_boundary: Manufacturing compatibility and whole-start BOM are mapped from the synthetic annual catalog. Actual receipt/qualification dates are declared independently; the annual six-cell supply and maintenance trajectories are not imported or jointly executed.

qualified_staffing.information_clock: Dated qualified parts and annual/monthly provider capacity gate physical admission. Only actual prior completed service qualifies staffing notice. A later failed support or replacement booking does not revoke binding notice. Site crews then reserve retained duties and funded overtime before actual awards.
qualified_staffing.resource_boundary: Provider support engineers, integration capacity and each legal operator site crew are separate. Outside annual reservations are unavailable capacity, not executed outside service, payroll or cash.
qualified_staffing.component_boundary: One synthetic catalog BOM per whole paid start, including rejected starts. A named actuator replacement is due in month4. Consigned parts and repair labor remain inside the existing paid manufacture/support bundles; their independent supplier cash or labor capacity is not modeled.
qualified_staffing.decision_gate: A removable paid block needs a forward qualified-service and fallback plan, not only purchased robots or one successful prior month. Check both cleaning and separately due inventory service.
limits: No actual BOM, support entitlement, staffing agreement, maintenance rate, payroll removal or all-service ROI is measured.
Eight monthly periods, deterministic installed-unit-first admission, fixed bids and no within-shift travel/deadlines; not an optimized portfolio or staffing policy.
The other five cells are measurement/decision boundaries, not numerically calibrated or jointly executed in this fixture.
Annual reservations carry no invented expense; outside inventory service and its payer are executed separately on the site crew. Do not sum these resource pools or service units.

contract.role_cash: Fixed allocations by logical role are summed when roles share one legal account; no capital appears on consolidation
contract.physical_integration: Integrator prepays commission plus first-month support; operator pays the integration/validation price and support passthrough atomically
contract.staff_and_site_costs: The target service operator pays target regular staffing, prospective overtime, overhead, materials and site software. The rival funds its own human crew. Each customer company retains customer contracts and service receipts.
contract.service_payment: The target customer company pays an explicit amount per accepted cleaning zone after delivery. The service scope includes its retained inventory duties; no additional inventory fee is assumed. Same-entity payments are eliminated.
contract.initial_model_work: Pre-admission paid review work replaces first-successful-admission development charges. Completed failed reviews remain paid. Setup, allocated development and upfront fee occur once per unit on first completed review; demonstration, adaptation, compute, validation and validation fee recur per completed attempt. Physical integration remains separately charged once at commissioning.
contract.recurring_model_work: Catalog inference multiplier, maintenance and network costs per supported unit-month; opaque robot digital bundle replaced
contract.resource_hours: Pre-admission reviews consume the same declared engineering/demonstration pools before commissioning; operating service never recharges that work. These are dedicated specialist resources, distinct from paid site crews and annual provider support.
contract.competition: Actual fixed-lot customer awards use paid qualified capacity and prior service. The rival is a digital-improved human business with no robot fleet; a second architecture contract is not inferred.

limits: All prices, funding, costs, resource pools and qualification gates are synthetic assumptions
No avoided-baseline cash credit, intrinsic architecture productivity multiplier or payroll-removal claim
Per-unit allocated model-development cash is an explicit scenario convention, not measured lab cash or optimal shared adaptation
No autonomous service-price negotiation, optimal capital allocation or asset recovery; standard cases use no debt
Real rights, compatible configuration, sustained quality and whole-system costs remain unknown
One architectural target and a human-led rival; two architectural fleets, optimal bids, shared adaptation and endogenous learning remain unimplemented.
Fixed logical-role capital is summed by legal entity. A fixed synthetic share price is not a comparable enterprise valuation across different opening target cash or outsourcing arrangements.

architecture_awards.cash_boundary: Internal model, integration and operator service prices redistribute cash. All-payer resource/transaction cash includes the architecture resource supplier exactly once.
architecture_awards.title_boundary: The architectural service operator buys and owns target robots. Acquiring the customer company does not transfer separately owned operator assets or pool its crew/cash.
architecture_awards.scope: One selected architecture on the target; the rival is human-led. Each complete case has one physical, part, provider-resource, crew, Treasury and customer-award history.

development.rights_scope: Explicit collection/use premises for fresh named review evidence and one configuration/unit. No cross-company data rights, transferred license, learned capability or empirical validation is inferred.
development.timing: Mandatory payroll/debt settle before phase-3 review prepayment. A completed precommission review consumes dedicated specialist engineering and demonstration capacity in a declared pre-service window. Phase-4 physical commissioning and provider resources remain separate. A blocked booking performs no work; a completed failed review is never rolled back by later admission failure.
development.service_boundary: Review evidence is neither customer service nor training output. The outcome is a declared hypothesis, not a simulated acceptance trial or measured learning effect. Existing service capability and crew policies remain unchanged after a declared pass.
development.cash_boundary: Review fees are internal-party transfers; external review resources are included once in all-payer resource cash. Cancelled unperformed work differs from paid failed work. Hardware may remain stranded after stopping, so no lifecycle ROI is reported.
development.decision: Compare the next funded attempt with a qualified human-led service policy. Prior paid failure belongs in history and does not supply engineering capacity, rights, qualification or a reason to continue.
limits: One target configuration and unit, deterministic declared outcomes and fixed eight-month bids; not an optimized development stopping policy.
No detailed robot trial dynamics, trial wear/parts, paid staff for a full external lab, stochastic learning curve or current project prices.
The distinct automotive learning fixture is not imported or added to this cleaning-service world. Shared adaptation, configuration changes and commercial alternative qualification remain open.
